basics.name: Marcelo Rondon
basics.label: Product Designer, Human-Centered AI Systems
basics.summary: Product designer focused on design systems and human-centered AI tools. I build and run what I design: deterministic code does everything it can, the model gets the smallest trustworthy job, and human approval sits where the consequences are. Recent work includes in-house AI automations that replaced 3–5 hours of weekly video editing, Ghosted, an AI-assisted job-application product used by real testers, and Daybreak, a local-first Mac and iPhone planner with an auditable agent layer.

work.name: Asheville Dispensary
highlights: Lead product and brand design for three brands (Asheville Dispensary, Plantbar, Nightshade) across web, print and packaging, anchored by a shared Figma design system.

Built an automated product-to-social video pipeline that replaced 3–5 hours a week of manual video editing: when a new flower drop is announced in Slack, an AI agent pulls each product's data, generates branded cards and vertical story videos, files them in Asana and queues them for social approval, with duplicate protection, quiet hours and a go-live check so nothing posts early.

Cut the pipeline's running cost about 60% by redesigning when and how it runs: a lightweight model screens for new drops and hands off to a stronger one only when there's work, measured with a per-run usage report.

Built several more in-house AI automations and systems that expand our design system and assets: presentations generated from approved templates, packaging checks against compliance checklists, and print coordination from approved artwork to vendor pickup, with people approving every step that matters.
Designed and built an internal asset-management tool in React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS that gives marketing and operations one place to find, manage and preserve brand assets.
Design and ship reusable UI components into WordPress through custom PHP and JavaScript plugins, closing the gap between mockups and production.

work.name: VegAvengers Marketing
highlights: Designed and shipped a responsive discovery experience with flexible search across VegFests, animal sanctuaries, locations, dates, months, and changing event states.
Evolved the product into a hybrid Astro and Payload architecture: prerendered editorial pages, live resource-search APIs, and a headless CMS backed by Postgres with media in Cloudflare R2.

Defined debounced, selective rebuild policies plus fixture and Astro DB fallback paths so content changes avoid unnecessary deploys and the public experience degrades safely if Payload is unavailable.

projects.name: Ghosted
projects.description: An AI-assisted job-application workspace, designed and shipped across three versions and now live with real testers.
highlights: Designed and shipped Ghosted through three versions — a Go terminal prototype, a Next.js web app backed by 744 tests, and a 2026 rebuild around a live React + Typst resume canvas — now used by real testers.

Kept the model's job small and checkable: platform APIs, parsing and validation run in code first; the AI only drafts, and every resume change arrives as a versioned, highlighted edit the person accepts or rejects.
Designed the agent to interview for evidence instead of inventing it: it asks for specifics, writes bullets only from what the person said, and names gaps against each posting.
Built job intake across Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, Amazon and Microsoft APIs with Firecrawl as a fallback, trimming postings to the role, requirements, pay and benefits.
Run it in production for testers: personal-code accounts, server sync and backups, an admin console, and in-app feedback with screenshots routed to Discord.

projects.name: Daybreak
projects.description: Designed and built a local-first personal planning product for Mac and iPhone that combines a deterministic planning engine with agent-assisted adjustments while keeping the plan editable and the user in control.
highlights: Shipped a shared SwiftUI and SwiftData app for macOS and iPhone with private CloudKit sync, without a product account or hosted application server
Separated a pure, testable planning engine from the app layer so generated day plans obey explicit schedule, ownership, and local-day boundary rules
Defined typed UI-agent parity contracts so agent-accessible actions match the product grammar, emit auditable receipts, and leave destructive or external actions behind explicit safety exclusions
Kept automated planning inspectable and editable: people can review, move, defer, or remove Daybreak-owned blocks while source-owned calendar meetings remain protected
Dogfooded the product against real planning and sync failures, turning trust problems into tested product rules across Mac and iPhone
